---
title: "Designing a clearer portfolio with CSS / SCSS"
description: "A practical guide to the styling choices used on this website."
---

## Why appearance matters to a visitor

A recruiter should be able to identify my focus, find a project, and understand the evidence quickly. I use consistent colors, readable typography, spacing, and reusable components to make that path clear.

## CSS, SCSS, and HTML work together

**HTML** provides structure: headings, paragraphs, navigation, images, and links. **CSS** controls how those elements look. **SCSS** extends CSS with variables and nesting; Quarto compiles the SCSS into browser-ready CSS during rendering.

In this project, Markdown becomes HTML. Classes on Quarto divs connect the content to reusable style rules. The site's `styles.scss` contains Bootstrap theme variables in a `scss:defaults` section and custom rules in a `scss:rules` section.

## Apply a theme in Quarto

The `_quarto.yml` file connects the stylesheet to the website:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, styles.scss]
```

The dashboard declares the same theme under its own `format: dashboard` settings. That keeps the visual identity consistent across the website and dashboard.

## Set reusable SCSS variables

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$primary: #167d8d;
$body-bg: #f7f9fa;
$body-color: #17333b;
$font-family-sans-serif: "Segoe UI", Arial, sans-serif;
```

Changing `$primary` updates Bootstrap components that use the primary color. This is easier to maintain than repeating separate color values throughout the site.

## Build a reusable component

This HTML creates a card that a visitor can scan quickly:

```html
<div class="example-card">
  <h3>From survey to decision</h3>
  <p>Clear evidence helps a manager choose what to investigate next.</p>
</div>
```

The SCSS controls its presentation:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/
.example-card {
  border: 1px solid #bed5da;
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 1.25rem;
  background: white;
  box-shadow: 0 3px 12px #17333b0a;
}
```

### Live example

::: {.example-card}
### From survey to decision
Clear evidence helps a manager choose what to investigate next.
:::

## Make the site usable across screens

I use fluid page layouts, descriptive image text, visible keyboard focus, and responsive spacing. This rule reduces the homepage hero padding on small screens:

```scss
@media (max-width: 650px) {
  .hero { padding: 1.25rem; }
}
a:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #b96715;
  outline-offset: 3px;
}
```

The result is a portfolio whose design supports the content: a dark navigation bar anchors the site, teal highlights actions, and light backgrounds separate sections without competing with the charts.
